question: Why does an OS use paging instead of contiguous allocation?

beats.speaker: interviewer
beats.line: Why does an OS use paging instead of contiguous allocation?

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: Contiguous allocation needs one unbroken block, so free memory ends up as unusable gaps.
beats.source_quote: Contiguous allocation requires a single unbroken block of memory.

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: Paging splits memory into fixed-size frames, and any page can go in any free frame.
beats.source_quote: Paging splits memory into fixed-size frames.

beats.speaker: student
beats.line: So those scattered gaps become usable and external fragmentation disappears.
beats.source_quote: External fragmentation disappears once any page can go in any frame.
